what_you_do: You write your reading of a situation, look at it through three lenses, and sort the readings by fit.
why:
When something goes wrong, one reading can take over, like “It means I'm not good enough”, and shape how bad it feels. It may not be the only fair reading.

This is practice at finding other realistic readings and keeping the ones that fit.

method.name: Seeing it another way (reappraisal)
method.text: How we read a situation shapes how we feel. Reappraisal means finding other realistic readings, not pretending it's fine. One lens asks what you'd say to a friend (self-distancing); another asks what will matter in a month (temporal distancing).

research.text: A review of emotion-regulation experiments suggests that reconsidering what a situation means reduces negative feelings straight afterwards, with a small-to-moderate effect.
research.who: 306 experimental comparisons · settings to be confirmed from the full text

research.text: Research with 170 adults suggests reappraisal isn't always helpful: skill at it went with fewer depressive symptoms under stress people couldn't control, but more under stress they could. So this exercise asks whether you can act on the situation.
Experiments found that using your own name or “you” instead of “I” when talking to yourself lowered distress in stressful social tasks.
research.who: 585 people, mostly US students · 6 experiments, 2 of them online; distress measured in 2 lab experiments (first impressions, a speech)

research.text: Experiments found that picturing a recent stressful event from the distant future lowered distress, partly by highlighting that it's temporary.
research.who: University students thinking about their own recent stressors · 5 experiments, plus 2 that only measured

research.text: A large trial found that brief written reappraisal instructions, used once online, reduced negative feelings about the pandemic straight afterwards, compared with control.
research.who: 21,644 adults, 87 countries · used once online, measured straight afterwards

similar_note: The trial above gave one kind of reappraisal instruction for one topic. No research has tested an exercise with three lenses and a fit board like this one.
about_this_exercise: This exercise uses reappraisal, but this version hasn't been tested itself. The research above used other instructions.
limits: Seeing it differently doesn't change the situation; if you can act on it, planning a step may matter more.
Before-and-after ratings show how it feels now, not whether the exercise works.
